notes: Regenerate this file each session from git log and a fresh count of src/data/ — do not hand-edit numbers forward from a prior run.

Updated 2026-08-25 (second pass, same day): the security-privacy and QA audits that were missing in the first pass have been written to docs/review/ and are now the authoritative source for launch-blocker severity. Seven claimed fixes were independently re-verified against the code, not taken on report.

CRITICAL: two of the drafted security-fix migrations (20260825090000, 20260825091000) are confirmed via `npx supabase migration list` to be un-pushed to the live Supabase project. The admin-takeover trigger and the admin_notes exposure are still live in production. Nothing from this session's remediation is committed to git either — git log still ends at ee8b24f.

phases.name: Prototype churn
phases.summary: Three full rebuilds in three days (v4, v5, v6) before the stack settled. Nothing from this phase is user-visible in the current product.

phases.name: Core build: React PWA v7
phases.summary: Production React+TypeScript PWA (package.json version 7.0.0, still current). Guide expanded 15→25 spots. Species expanded 5→11. Photo species ID shipped. Ten days of no commits followed (2026-08-12 to 2026-08-21).

phases.name: Monetisation and ops scaffolding
phases.summary: Shop directory split from advertising. Owner console added with a 249-item review queue. Free/paid capability matrix built. docs/ROADMAP.md written and v1 scope frozen. Naming research killed three previously-favoured names via live search collision testing.

phases.name: Rebrand and accounts
phases.summary: Renamed GCF → Shorebound, moved to the root of shorebound.fish. Hosting moved from GitHub Pages to Cloudflare Workers. Accounts shipped in one commit (sign-up, sign-in, settings, owner console gate). Home page and narrative rewritten; tagline settled on 'Go Fish Yo'Self'.

phases.name: Hardening and handoff
phases.summary: Admin approval flow, CORS preflight fix, owner-vocabulary scrub from reader bundle, agent-swarm reconciliation. Six audits commissioned (architecture, backend, test-coverage, documentation, security-privacy, QA); the first four written to docs/review/ same day but never committed. The security-privacy and QA reports were returned but not written to disk until Phase 6.

phases.name: Same-day remediation of the two most serious findings (uncommitted)
phases.summary: Security-privacy review (NIST CSF 2.0, verdict NO-GO for launch/store submission, narrowed to PR-1/PR-2/PR-3) and QA review (verdict Blocked on C1/C2) written to docs/review/. Seven fixes made and independently verified against code: content-integrity inference removed from zones.ts (QA C1, the most serious finding of all six reviews), safety-label clarity in Cautions.tsx (QA I1), an admin-takeover migration requiring email confirmation (Backend C1), an admin_notes RLS/grant fix plus a previously-unknown broken-admin-writes bug found while fixing it (Security PR-2), a CORS production-origin fix for identify-fish (Security PR-3), an offline bypass for the account gate plus permanently ungating /care (Architecture C2), and a service-worker cache allowlist replacing a whole-origin Supabase cache rule (Security PR-6). Build clean, 340 tests passing across 18 files on the settled tree. NONE of this is committed (git log unchanged at ee8b24f). The two security-fixing migrations are confirmed NOT pushed to the live Supabase project via `supabase migration list` — both live vulnerabilities (admin takeover, admin_notes exposure) remain live in production.

v1_items.evidence: Name (Shorebound) and primary domain (shorebound.fish) are decided and live since Phase 4. Email is not working for real sign-ups (Supabase over_email_send_rate_limit); shorebound.app returns 525, never provisioned; gofishyoself.com redirect not configured. All three are owner-blocked. v1_items.evidence: src/pages/Privacy.tsx and src/pages/Support.tsx exist, are routed, and are substantive. Three confirmed defects (documentation + security-privacy reviews): states 'Hosting is GitHub Pages' (false since Phase 4, on an App Store 5.1.1(i) compliance page); SUPPORT_EMAIL points at the unconfirmed shorebound.app domain; and the page still says 'we have no record of you to produce, correct or delete' a few paragraphs after describing the account record it holds — pre-accounts language left in place.

v1_items.title: The shop directory, visible to readers
v1_items.evidence: Shipped in Phase 3. Two independent, both-confirmed offline failures from two different reviews: (a) Architecture C4 — useShopListings.ts filters the whole bundled 20-shop directory through a live Supabase read; offline, every shop disappears. Not fixed. (b) QA C2, the one CRITICAL item QA's verdict left open — 10/11 species images, 6/6 hazard images and 8/8 habitat photos are remote hotlinks outside the service worker's precache glob (jpg/jpeg/webp excluded); offline, the fish-ID plate and every Handle With Care card show a broken-image icon. Not fixed as of this writing.

v1_items.evidence: store/ contains one icon (icon-1024.png) and a logo-concepts folder. No per-device screenshots beyond one regeneration commit, no listing copy file, no age rating or category decision found.

blockers.title: refresh-conditions is invokable by anyone holding the public anon key, with no rate limit of its own
blockers.source: docs/review/security-privacy-review.md (PR-1); same underlying issue as docs/review/backend-review.md (I2)
blockers.summary: No rate-limiting, cooldown or ledger exists in refresh-conditions/index.ts. The JWT check that gates it accepts the same anon key shipped in the bundle. Unbounded invocation risks NOAA/NWS throttling the shared Supabase egress IP, degrading live tide/weather for every visitor. The one item both the security NO-GO and the QA Blocked verdict agree is the top open finding. Not fixed; no draft exists.

blockers.title: Offline-first fails on every species, hazard and habitat page
blockers.summary: 10/11 species images, 6/6 hazard images and 8/8 habitat photos are remote hotlinks outside the service worker's precache glob (jpg/jpeg/webp excluded). Offline, the fish-ID plate and every Handle With Care card render a broken-image icon — this is the safety content CLAUDE.md says must be led with. The other item both authoritative verdicts left open. Not fixed; QA notes a fix is planned next but it is not in this working tree.

blockers.source: docs/review/architecture-review.md (C1); restated as docs/review/security-privacy-review.md (GV-1) and docs/review/qa-review.md (I7) — three independent audits converging on one finding
blockers.summary: .github/workflows/deploy.yml still runs tests/typecheck/secret-grep against a GitHub Pages target nothing serves. wrangler deploy, the actual production path, is not gated by any of it. Not fixed.

blockers.title: Admin takeover via unconfirmed email match — FIXED IN CODE, NOT IN PRODUCTION
blockers.summary: Migration 20260825090000_admin_claim_requires_confirmed_email.sql drafted and confirmed correct by reading it (grants admin only on email_confirmed_at becoming non-null, retracts unconfirmed-held rows). Confirmed via `npx supabase migration list` against the live project that it has NOT been pushed (remote:"") while the original vulnerable trigger (20260823120000) is live. The vulnerability is live in production right now.

blockers.title: admin_notes readable by anyone with the anon key, plus a previously-unknown broken-admin-writes bug — FIXED IN CODE, NOT IN PRODUCTION
blockers.summary: Migration 20260825091000_lock_admin_notes_and_restore_admin_writes.sql drafted and confirmed correct (revokes blanket SELECT, adds admin_list_shop_listings()/admin_list_ad_campaigns() security-definer RPCs, confirmed called from src/admin/Shops.tsx and Ads.tsx). Confirmed NOT pushed to the live database by the same migration-list check. Latent in production today (no rate has been typed into admin_notes yet). The same migration also restores insert/update/delete grants to authenticated, fixing a silently-broken owner-console Save that no audit had previously found.

blockers.summary: Runtime cache rule narrowed from the whole Supabase origin to an explicit endpoint allowlist; src/test/sw.cache.test.ts guards against widening. Confirmed in code. Bundle-level fix, takes effect on next deploy once committed.

blockers.title: Per-species casting advice was inferred, not researched — FIXED IN CODE, not deployed

Confirmed no cast-zone line renders anywhere currently — correct per the content rule (empty beats invented), but worth naming as a content gap, not a defect.

on_track: No single day of building was wasted, and the response to the two audits missing from the first pass was fast and largely correct: six of seven claimed code-level fixes were independently re-verified against the source and hold up. But 'fixed' and 'shipped' are not the same claim, and the gap between them is the most important fact in this update: nothing from this remediation session is committed to git, and — confirmed directly against the live Supabase project via `supabase migration list`, not taken on report — the two migrations that close the two most serious backend security findings (admin takeover, admin_notes exposure) have NOT been pushed. Both vulnerabilities are live in production right now, exactly as the security review found them, regardless of what the local working tree contains. Set that aside and the underlying shape is unchanged: v1 is not close on its own six-item list (store packaging and the wrappers not started at all; the shop directory now has two independent, confirmed ways to fail offline rather than one), and the two findings both authoritative verdicts (security NO-GO, QA Blocked) still call open — refresh-conditions's unbounded invocation, and every species/hazard/habitat photo breaking offline — are exactly the class of bug this project's own lesson says is invisible in source and obvious in a browser or a live request; neither has been checked that way yet. This should not be read as a criticism of the remediation itself, which was fast and correct where it went — it should be read as: nothing here is closed until it is committed, pushed to the live database where that applies, and checked against the running system rather than the diff.
